text: Hello, boys and girls.I'm Julianne.Nice to see you again.Are you ready for the class?Now, let's get started.First, read and match.Make, Cakes, A is pronounced as A.And, Can, A is pronounced as A.Peter, Eva, E is pronounced as E.Clever, Eggs, E is pronounced as A.Go on, Like, Drive, I is pronounced as I.Fish, Skip, I is pronounced as I.Puppets, Butter, U is pronounced as U.Super, Youth, U is pronounced as U.Chopsticks, Oranges, O is pronounced as O.Rope, Coke, O is pronounced as O.Super, boys and girls, look, these words find their new friends and make two new sentences.Super, Peter likes cakes, eggs, oranges, fish, butter, and coke.Well done.Clever, Eva, can make puppets, use chopsticks, skip a rope, and drive.Fantastic.Kitty and her classmates visited Old MacDonald's farm.What is on the farm?Look and say by yourselves.Super, boys and girls, Kitty likes the farm very much.At night, she had a dream about it.Let's dub.Well done, children.Look, this is Uncle Lee.He has a farm too.The students want to visit his farm.Guess what is on his farm.Take out your workbook and turn to page 68.Task A.Think, Say, and Write.Kitty thinks and says, there are some dogs and cats on the farm.So she writes, can you think, say, and write by yourselves?Are you finished?Now let's share.Maybe there are some dogs, cats, hens, chicks, ducks, pigs, sheep, rabbits, and many other animals on the farm.Look, they are on the farm now.What do they see?Take out your workbook again and turn to page 66.Part F.Read and Circle.Get your pencils ready.Now let's check the answers.What's this?Good job, it's a pig.What are these?Yes, they are dogs.Are they hens?Yes, they are.Peepee, what are they?They are chicks.The students see many animals on the farm, but how many?Still on this page, part E, look and write.There are four chicks, three hens, six ducks, five cats, seven dogs, and two pigs on the farm.Wow, so many animals on the farm.Can you read?Can you answer?Yes, they are chicks.Number two.Good job, they are yellow.Number three.Yes, they are small.Number four.What can they do?Good job, they can run fast.And the last question, listen.What food do they like?They like corn.Yes, they like corn.Follow me, corn.Chicks like corn.What animals like corn, too?Hens like corn.Ducks like corn.Pigs like corn, too.Now look.Here, chicks is about the name of the farm animals.Yellow is about the color.Small is about the feature.Run fast is about the ability.And corn is about the food that they like.This is Kitty's information card.Can you help Ben finish his?Look, what are they?What color are they?Brown.How are they?Lovely.They can run fast.They like dog food.Dogs like bones, too.Now it's your turn to choose the farm animals that you like and complete your information card.Super boys and girls.Now you have your own information card.It's time to talk.Look at Alice's information card.Let's be Alice and talk about the hens.They are hens.They are orange.They are fat.They can lay eggs.Now can you look at your information cardNow it's your turn to say something about the farm animals that you like.Well done, boys and girls.Now you know how to talk.Finally, you can draw and write.Please take out your workbookand take a look at the information card.This is her writing.The first sentence is the beginning.This is the body part, which is composed of the name, the color or the feature, the ability, and the food.The last sentence is the ending.Are you clear?It's your turn to draw and
